Subject: Capacity planning for renewal

Hi Lauren —

We are looking at our renewal window in June and want to add headroom for holiday traffic next season. Current committed pool is 4x A100 equivalents; we'd like to discuss adding 2 more GPUs to the reserved pool and formalizing per-pool throughput guarantees (tokens/sec) so our SREs can align monitoring.

Can you share an SLO proposal (tokens/sec per pool, burst behavior, ramp schedule) and the impact on pricing for a 12-month extension + +2 GPU add-on? Happy to do a short call today if that helps.

Thanks,
Asha

Hi Asha —

Thanks — we can put together a short addendum that (1) extends the term 12 months from your renewal date, (2) reserves an additional 2x A100-equivalent GPUs in your Dedicated pool, and (3) defines per-pool throughput guarantees and burst rules. High-level proposal below; I'll attach a formal SOW & pricing after you confirm the approach.

Summary proposal (draft):
- Reserved capacity: +2x A100-equivalent GPUs (so total reserved pool = 6x).
- Baseline TPS guarantee: 28,000 tokens/sec sustained per reserved pool (measured as aggregate successful token output across all nodes in the pool, 1s sampling, 24h windows).
- Burst window: up to 62,000 tokens/sec aggregate for a contiguous 10-minute window per day; bursts above baseline are subject to token-burst accounting.
- Ramp schedule: additional GPUs come online during the first 7 days of the renewal; we will provision staging capacity prior to term start and perform a controlled traffic ramp (10% increments, 2-hour holds) to verify KV cache warm-up and kernel selection.
- Fallback policy: if reserved pool unavailable, traffic will failover to your Dedicated backup pool (if enabled) or Redwood-hosted fallback model with reduced TPS; documented remediation credits (see below).
- SLO / credits: availability SLO computed as % of 1-minute samples meeting baseline TPS across 30-day windows. If monthly availability < 99.5% we propose service credits prorated against the monthly Dedicated fee (credit tiers to be detailed in addendum).

Pricing impact: incremental committed fee for +2 GPUs and the 12-month term summarized in an attached pricing delta (includes token accounting for burst).

If that aligns, I'll circulate SOW v3 and the reserved_pool_tps_schedule workbook for your SREs to review. Can we schedule a 30-minute call at 1:30pm PT today to walk through?

Best,
Lauren Bishop

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Date: 2027-05-14T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity planning for renewal — SLO wording and rollback mechanics

Lauren / Marissa —

Asha's ask looks good; a couple of product/legal points we should tighten before sending to customer:

1) SLO definition: recommend wording — "Baseline throughput SLO: the reserved pool will sustain >= 28,000 tokens/sec aggregated across the pool, measured by successful token emissions per 1s sample, with a 30-day rolling evaluation period." Keep measurement and window explicit.

2) Burst accounting: define how burst tokens are billed and how they contribute to capacity events. Suggest a separate 'burst bucket' with daily allocation (e.g., 600k tokens/day) and per-minute cap tied to the 10-minute burst limit.

3) Remediation credits: propose three tiers tied to 30-day availability: <99.5% = 5% monthly credit, <99.0% = 10%, <98.0% = 20%. Credits should not exceed monthly committed fee. Also include operational remedies (priority incident bridge, 4-hour response for P1).

4) Rollout / rollback: include a canary and automatic fallback: canary at 5% traffic for 2 hours, then 25%, 50%, full. If performance deviates >10% from expected TPS during canary hold, auto-rollback to previous pool config.

I'll draft SLO and credit language; LMK if you want me to put this into SOW text.

-Karthik
Senior Product Manager — Redwood Inference

Thanks Lauren — that draft looks reasonable. A few clarifications from our side:

- Can you confirm the measurement endpoint? Our SREs will want to pull the same datapoints; prefer a public metric name (e.g., redwood.reserved_pool.tokens_per_sec.<pool_id>) in CloudWatch/Prometheus.
- Confirm the daily burst bucket number (you suggested 600k tokens/day) and whether unused burst credits roll over.
- Pricing: happy to accept the incremental fee but will need a formal quote and PO by next week for finance.

If you can send the SOW + pricing and the HubSpot/DocuSign link, we'll route to procurement today. We authorize the +2 GPUs pending final SOW language.

Best,
Asha
